_comment: Respuestas para la postulacion al DPG Registry. El repositorio publicgoods-candidates fue archivado en 2024; este archivo ya no se sube; es la fuente desde la que se copian los datos al portal https://app.digitalpublicgoods.net/signup. Estructura conservada del esquema oficial por claridad. ACTUALIZADO 2026-07-30: la descripcion decia que no se almacenan datos personales de donantes, y dejo de ser cierto al enviarse el pre-registro en linea de donaciones. Ver 'privacy_note' abajo.
name: Araguaney
description: Free and open-source software for humanitarian aid collection centers. It registers in-kind donations item by item with quality rules (WHO medicine donation guidelines), packs them into homogeneous boxes with QR codes, consolidates them into pallets and shipments with a customs-ready manifest, and aggregates the stock of every connected center into a national dashboard. It stores no data whatsoever about aid recipients. At the collection center a donation is anonymous by default — recording the donor is an optional checkbox someone has to tick on purpose — while registering a donation online does require a name and email, because that is where the QR code and the link to modify or cancel it are sent. Donor data is covered by a published privacy notice with declared retention periods, automatic purge of unconfirmed records and self-service deletion.

SDGs.evidenceText: Target 11.5 aims to significantly reduce the losses caused by disasters. Araguaney addresses the logistics failure that delays in-kind relief: without a shared standard, each collection center records donations its own way, boxes are packed without criteria, and shipments stall at customs for lack of a manifest. By standardizing item-level intake, homogeneous boxes with QR traceability, and exportable packing lists, relief supplies reach affected populations faster and in usable condition.

Targets 17.16 and 17.17 promote multi-stakeholder partnerships. Araguaney gives independent collection centers, civil society organizations and coordination bodies a common registration standard and a shared national dashboard, so organizations that would otherwise operate in isolation can see aggregate stock and coordinate shipments. The software is free to use and open source, removing cost as a barrier to participation.

privacy_note.why: Between the submission (2026-07-27) and this update, the platform shipped donor pre-registration: a person can register what they plan to donate before dropping it off, receive a QR code, and edit or cancel it. That path requires a name and an email — there would be nowhere to send the code otherwise — so the earlier claim of storing no donor personal data no longer holds. In-person intake is unchanged: anonymous by default, with donor details behind an optional checkbox.
privacy_note.indicator_6_data_extraction: Unchanged for aid recipients: none of their data exists in the system. Exports (manifest PDF/XLSX, reports CSV) contain inventory, not personal data. Donor data is never part of an export and never appears on a public page — the QR page of a donation shows its status and contents, never who sent it.
privacy_note.indicator_7_privacy_and_laws: Compliance now rests on a regime rather than on absence of data: privacy notice (ES/EN) with a dedicated donor category stating what is collected, why and whether it is required; declared retention periods per data type; an automatic purge job that expires unconfirmed pre-registrations and strips the donor's personal data when no live or delivered donation justifies keeping it; self-service account deletion for platform users; and ARCO rights with a published contact. Aligned with Mexico's LFPDPPP.
privacy_note.indicator_9_do_no_harm: Strengthened: in-kind donation is a known trade-based money-laundering channel, so the platform added an irrevocable-transfer acceptance recorded with its version, structural controls (a donor cannot designate the consignee nor trace goods to destination, and pallets are mixed by design), an escalation queue for unusual-volume captures resolved by coordination and never by whoever captured it, and a published red-flag guide for coordinators. Scope is deliberately proportionate per FATF R.8: recording and escalation, no sanctions screening or documentary identity verification.
